subject: Biology
central_question: How do plants grow, differentiate and develop under the combined control of internal regulators and environmental conditions?
in_scope_units: Growth as an irreversible increase and the indeterminate nature of plant growth.
Arithmetic and geometric growth, sigmoid curves and growth rates.
Characteristics and discovery of plant growth regulators.
Effects of auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, ethylene and ABA.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any increase in size is biological growth.
known_pitfalls.correction: Plant growth is irreversible, permanent and associated with living metabolism.

known_pitfalls.claim: All daughter cells of a meristem remain capable of division.
known_pitfalls.correction: Many lose division capacity and differentiate into the plant body.

known_pitfalls.claim: Each PGR has only one fixed effect.
known_pitfalls.correction: PGRs have diverse, overlapping, synergistic and antagonistic actions.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 1 for core definitions.
Use NCERT Exercise 3 to compare growth patterns and rates.
Use NCERT Exercise 4 to organise PGR discovery and applications.
Use NCERT Exercise 8 to select PGRs for practical responses.
Use NCERT Exercise 10 to predict outcomes of GA3, ethylene and cytokinin changes.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter EXERCISES section contains Questions 1-10 on growth patterns, differentiation, PGRs, photoperiodic responses and applied predictions.
